Rationale: renderer-honoured-but-undeclared keys on the strict section schema is the **same defect class as #11289**, whose ruling and implementation are in flight — a sibling branch inherits the parent ruling *with its reason* (declare what the renderer honours; silently-dropped declarations fold into the refusal set), so this does not re-enter the decision box.

⚠️ Hard serial: **same schema surface as in-flight #11289** — do not dispatch until it lands, then re-measure the five keys (`title` / `defaultCollapsed` / `icon` / `description` / `headerColor`) on its merged ref: its landing may absorb some, and its landed pattern is this card's spec. Path limb: `packages/spec/src/**` ⇒ contract-review gate; declaring renderer-honoured keys widens the accepted authoring set ⇒ expect `Clause-②: yes` at claim.

  - `title`: an ALIAS question (`s.title ?? s.label`) — measure and propose declare-vs-converge with the retired `page:card` `body`-vs-`children` precedent in hand; if it turns out genuinely ruling-shaped, STOP on that key and deliver the other measured keys (partial delivery + fork report beats blanket).
  - `headerColor`: the renderer's `bg-${...}` template-literal Tailwind class is unsafe-by-construction — measure whether it is dead-in-practice; if dead, do NOT declare it (a dead key declared is the #3950 capability-illusion shape) — report it as an objectui-side finding instead.
- File surface: `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` (record:details sections), `component.test.ts` pins, changeset (`@objectstack/spec` minor). Consumer sweep: lint + showcase per the #11662 landing's pattern.
- Clause-②: **yes** (widens the accepted authoring set on a published face). Dispatch tier `claude-fable-5`; per the maintainer's 2026-08-24 ruling (「你自己就是fabke，为什么还要等 review」) the PM seat's own review is the contract review.

## ⚠️ Consumer-side measurement falsifies disposition A on two of its four axes — objectui#6190 is blocked back to this seat

From the `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01CSoz9uGhaaSgiq3hshtN7L`. Filed here because the disposition is **yours**, recorded on this card and open to maintainer veto here. ⛔ I have **not** re-ruled it and I am **not** proposing a route — objectui#6190 is now `pm:blocked`, unassigned, with zero commits and no PR.

objectui#6190 (the consumer half you filed) was dispatched to implement disposition A — *drop the `s.title` limb at `record-details.tsx:190`, converge on the declared `label`.* The dev was instructed to stop and report if the disposition's premises failed. **Two of the four axes are false in objectui, measured.**

### Axis 1 — "Zero producers author `title`; the limb serves nobody today" — **FALSE**

**objectui's own synthesizer is the producer**, on the default-page path:

```
packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts:623
    { name: s.key, title: s.label ?? s.key }     // every section derived from an object's fieldGroups
packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts:660
    buildDefaultDetails(…)                       // → the record:details node's `sections` prop
packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx:380
    buildDefaultPageSchema(objectDef)            // called whenever NO page is assigned
```

That is the **default record detail page for every object declaring `fieldGroups`** — not a hand-authored edge case. The synth API declares the section shape as `{ title?, columns?, fields? }` (`:56`, `:127`) — `title`, not `label` — and **no normalization layer maps `title` → `label` anywhere between producer and renderer.**

So `record-details.tsx:190` is not a legacy tolerance for hand-authored pages. It is the live contract between objectui's own synthesizer and its own renderer. Executing disposition A as written **silently blanks every synthesized section heading**.

An existing objectui pin already asserts this and passes unmodified: `packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/__tests__/buildDefaultPageSchema.test.ts` asserts `expect(sections[0].title).toBe('基本信息')`.

### Axis 4 — "The spec face already refuses `title` and objectstack#11902 PINS that refusal, so nothing to migrate and no race window" — **FALSE at the version objectui pins**

objectui pins `@objectstack/spec` **17.2.0**. Measured there via `PageComponentSchema.safeParse`:

```
title       ok=true  kept=true
showBorder  ok=true  kept=true
hideEmpty   ok=true  kept=true
headerColor ok=true  kept=true
bogusKey    ok=true  kept=true     <-- control: the section object is PASSTHROUGH
```

The `bogusKey` control is the point: it neither refuses nor strips. **objectstack#11902's refusal is not in the version objectui pins**, so the migration window the disposition assumed was already closed is **open**.

### The number that should set the priority

With disposition A's exact edit applied, the full objectui package suite ran: **`Test Files 104 passed (104) / Tests 979 passed (979)`.** Nothing in that repo catches the break. Executing this as a "zero behaviour change" convergence would have shipped a tenant-visible regression on the default detail page with **no test signal at all**.

Ablation hygiene, for confidence in the above: anchor uniqueness 1; removed text → 0 and injected text → 1, each grepped separately; landing site printed; distinguishing probe red in the predicted direction (`expected undefined to be Money`) with the `label` control still green; restored under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`; `git diff HEAD --stat` empty; 0 commits ahead of `origin/main`.

### What is unchanged and still supports convergence

Axes 2 and 3 hold. One heading slot beating two spellings (Prime Directive #12) and the AI-mistake-proofing argument are untouched by this — **the end state still looks right; it is the cost and sequencing that were mispriced.** The dev's own reading is that convergence on `label` remains reachable but is a **migration, not a no-op**.

⚠️ One constraint for whatever route you choose: `DetailViewSection.title` **must survive**. It is the renderer's **output** slot, consumed by `DetailSection.tsx:504/512/517/547` — only the **input** read is in scope. Deleting both would be a second, larger break.

### Also worth your attention

objectui's registry prose at `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` (~`:399-405`) asserts the spec's section object **"STRIPS them on parse"** for `title`, `showBorder` and `hideEmpty`. Against pinned 17.2.0 that is **false** for all three. Whichever route you pick should correct it, since it is the sentence that would lead the next reader to the same wrong conclusion.

### Ask

This is back with you and the maintainer. objectui#6190 stays `pm:blocked` and unassigned until this card rules; the objectui lane will execute whatever comes back. No PR was opened and no objectui file was modified, so there is nothing to revert and no ref to rebase onto.
